prompt: Build Spreadsheet, a small spreadsheet that runs as one self-contained HTML page with no server, no build step and no libraries. A tab bar across the top switches between twenty views, one per feature; the Grid view is the sheet itself. Grid: a table of cells addressed A1, B2, AB10; click a cell to select it, type in the formula bar above the grid and press Enter to set it; the cell shows its computed, formatted value. Parser: formulas start with '=' and hold numbers, strings in double quotes, TRUE/FALSE, cell references, ranges A1:B3, references into another sheet Sheet2!A1, named ranges, function calls, the operators + - * / ^ & = <> < > <= >= and unary minus, with parentheses. Calc: every cell recomputed from the raw texts, across sheets, in dependency order. Functions: SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX, COUNT, COUNTA, IF, AND, OR, NOT, ROUND, ABS, LEN, UPPER, LOWER, CONCAT, TRIM, MOD, SQRT, POWER, INT. Deps: the dependency graph, evaluation order, cycle detection, the dependents of a cell. Errors: #DIV/0!, #REF!, #NAME?, #VALUE!, #CYCLE!, #PARSE! shown in the cell, explained in the Errors view with a count per code. Format: number, percent, currency and general display with a decimals count, plus bold, italic and alignment per cell. History: undo and redo of every change, fifty steps deep. Rows and columns: insert and delete a row or a column with every formula reference in the sheet rewritten, a reference to a deleted cell becoming #REF!. Fill: fill down a range from its first row, continuing number and date series and shifting relative references. Find: find text in cells and replace it. CSV: export a range as CSV and import CSV text at a cell. Chart: a bar chart of a data range with a label range, drawn as inline SVG. Validation: a rule per cell (number range, list of allowed values, date) with the current violations listed. Names: named ranges usable in formulas. Sheets: several sheets in one book, add, rename, remove, switch, with cross-sheet references. Conditional: formatting rules over a range (greater than, less than, between, equal, contains) that add a CSS class to matching cells. Stats: count, sum, average, min and max of a range, like a status bar. Persist: the book saved to localStorage under a versioned schema, restored on load, with an older version-1 document migrated. Keys: arrow keys, Enter, Tab, Shift+Tab, Home and Ctrl+Home move the selection inside the sheet's bounds.
definition_of_done: final_output_file: spreadsheet.html, one self-contained HTML page. All 22 cases in test_acceptance.py pass via `python -I -m unittest discover -s . -v` with exit code 0. The page starts with <!doctype html>, makes zero external requests, holds a <nav> with one button[data-tab=NAME] and one <section id="panel-NAME"> per feature, an <input id="formula"> formula bar, and one plain <script id="app"> (not a module) that runs to completion in node with document, window and localStorage stubbed and leaves window.App.features holding one entry per feature, each with a `model` object of pure functions and a `render(root, state)` function. Twenty feature tests, one per feature, call the model functions listed in the contract with a fixed two-sheet book and check exact results: new objects, never mutated inputs; the evaluator's value for every cell of the fixture; cross-sheet and named references; the six error codes and their propagation; reference rewriting on row and column insertion and deletion; fill series; CSV quoting; an undo stack capped at fifty; a version-1 document migrated to version 2.
contract: Return ONE complete HTML document in the `code` field, from <!doctype html> to </html>, saved as spreadsheet.html. Structure: 1. <head> with a <style> holding every rule; no external stylesheet. 2. <body> with a <nav id="tabs"> holding one <button data-tab="NAME"> per feature and a <main> holding one empty <section id="panel-NAME" class="panel"> per feature, in this order: grid, parser, calc, functions, deps, errors, format, history, rowscols, fill, find, csv, chart, validation, names, sheets, conditional, stats, persist, keys. 3. One plain <script id="app"> (no type="module", no import or export) that builds a global `App` and ends with `window.App = App`. It must touch no DOM element and read no user data at load time: the gate extracts this script alone, stubs document, window, localStorage, location and history with inert objects, runs it in node and then calls the model functions listed below. Mounting (rendering every panel into its section, wiring the tabs, re-rendering on state changes, loading saved data) happens in App.mount(document), called from a second, separate <script> placed after it. 4. App.store = {get(), set(patch), subscribe(fn)} holding the book {sheets: [], active: <sheet id>, names: {}, ui: {selected: 'A1'}}; set merges the patch into the book and notifies subscribers. App.router.show(name) makes section#panel-NAME and its tab active and hides the others. 5. App.features.NAME = {model: {...}, render(root, state)} for each of the twenty names. render writes the feature's whole panel into root (its section) from state and wires its own events, which change state only through App.store.set. model holds pure functions: no DOM, no localStorage (persist excepted), never mutating the objects they receive, always returning new ones. GRID PANEL, what the browser gate clicks: a <table> with one <td data-addr="A1"> per cell showing format.model.display(value, style.format) and carrying the classes conditional.model.classes gives it; a click on a td selects it (class 'selected', ui.selected = its address); <input id="formula"> above the table holds the selected cell's raw text, and a keydown Enter on it sets that cell through grid.model.set and pushes history; a keydown ArrowUp/Down/Left/Right, Enter, Tab, Shift+Tab, Home, Ctrl+Home on a td or the table moves the selection with keys.model.next. Every change to cells, formats, rules, names or sheets is saved with persist.model.save. DATA. A book is {sheets: [sheet], active: <sheet id>, names: {NAME: 'Sheet1!A1:A2'}, ui: {}}. A sheet is {id, name, cells: {ADDR: {raw: string}}, formats: {ADDR: style}, rules: {ADDR: rule}, conditional: [rule]}; only non-empty cells are present in cells. ADDR is column letters then a 1-based row: A1, Z9, AA10; columns are 0-based numbers in the API (A = 0). A raw text starting with '=' is a formula; otherwise a text matching /^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$/ is a number, TRUE or FALSE (any case) a boolean, a leading apostrophe marks literal text, anything else is a string. A computed value is a number, a string, a boolean, null (an empty cell or a reference to one) or an error code string: '#DIV/0!', '#REF!', '#NAME?', '#VALUE!', '#CYCLE!', '#PARSE!'. In arithmetic null is 0 and a numeric string is its number, any other string is #VALUE!; in & (concatenation) null is ''; comparisons give booleans, numbers compare numerically and strings case-insensitively; ^ is right-associative (2^3^2 = 512) and binds tighter than unary minus, which binds tighter than * /, then + -, then &, then comparisons. An error in any operand or argument is the result (the first error met), except IF, which returns the chosen branch whatever the other holds. A range outside a function is #VALUE!. A reference to a sheet or a name that does not exist is #REF!/#NAME?. Cross-sheet references name the sheet as written (case-insensitive). A cell in a cycle, or depending on one, is #CYCLE!. Graph keys and the targets of names are '<sheet name>!<ADDR>' and '<sheet name>!<ADDR>:<ADDR>'. MODEL FUNCTIONS THE GATE CALLS, exact names and shapes: grid.model.toAddr(col, row) -> 'A1' from 0-based numbers; grid.model.parseAddr(text) -> {col, row} 0-based or null (A0, 1A and '' are null); grid.model.colName(col) -> 'A'..'Z','AA'; grid.model.get(sheet, addr) -> the raw text, '' when empty; grid.model.set(sheet, addr, raw) -> new sheet, an empty raw removing the cell; grid.model.range('B2:C3') -> ['B2','C2','B3','C3'] in row-major order, a reversed range normalised; grid.model.bounds(sheet) -> {cols, rows}: the count of columns and rows in use ({cols: 0, rows: 0} for an empty sheet). parser.model.isFormula(raw) -> raw starts with '='; parser.model.parse(raw) -> an AST: {type: 'num', value}, {type: 'str', value}, {type: 'bool', value}, {type: 'ref', sheet: null | 'Sheet2', addr: 'A1'}, {type: 'range', sheet, from: 'A1', to: 'B2'}, {type: 'name', name}, {type: 'call', name: 'SUM' (upper-cased), args: [ast]}, {type: 'bin', op, left, right}, {type: 'un', op: '-', arg}; an invalid formula gives {type: 'error', code: '#PARSE!'} instead of throwing; parser.model.refs(ast) -> the references as written ('A1:B2', 'Sheet2!A1', 'C4') in order of appearance. calc.model.compute(book) -> {<sheet id>: {ADDR: value}} for every non-empty cell of every sheet. functions.model.call(NAME, args) -> the value; args are computed values, a range argument being a flat array of its values; SUM, AVERAGE (alias AVG), MIN, MAX, COUNT use the numbers only and skip null, strings and booleans (MIN/MAX of no number: 0, AVERAGE of no number: #DIV/0!); COUNTA counts the non-null values; IF(cond, a, b); AND, OR over every value; NOT; ROUND(x, d) rounds half away from zero on the decimal text (ROUND(2.345, 2) = 2.35, not the float artefact 2.34); ABS, LEN, UPPER, LOWER, CONCAT (null is ''), TRIM, MOD, SQRT, POWER, INT (floor); an unknown name is #NAME?; an error among the arguments is returned as is, except by IF; functions.model.names() -> the sorted list of names. deps.model.graph(book) -> {key: [key]} with one key per non-empty cell, a formula's list holding every cell it reads (ranges and names expanded, in address order), a value cell holding []; deps.model.order(graph) -> keys in an order where every key comes after its dependencies; deps.model.cycles(graph) -> the sorted keys that lie on a cycle; deps.model.dependents(graph, key) -> the sorted keys that depend on key directly or transitively. errors.model.isError(value) -> boolean; errors.model.codes() -> the six codes; errors.model.describe(code) -> one sentence, '' for an unknown code; errors.model.summary(values) -> {code: count} over one sheet's computed values, codes with no occurrence left out. format.model.display(value, fmt) -> string: fmt is {kind: 'general' | 'number' | 'percent' | 'currency' | 'text', decimals} and may be missing (general); general shows a number with float noise removed (0.1+0.2 -> '0.3', 12 -> '12'), number with thousands separators and the decimals (1234.567, 0 -> '1,235'), percent multiplies by 100 and appends % (0.256, 1 -> '25.6%'), currency prefixes $ with thousands separators (1234.5, 2 -> '$1,234.50'); null -> '', booleans -> 'TRUE' / 'FALSE', errors and non-numeric strings as they are; format.model.styleOf(sheet, addr) -> {bold, italic, align: 'auto' | 'left' | 'center' | 'right', format: {kind, decimals}} with defaults {bold: false, italic: false, align: 'auto', format: {kind: 'general', decimals: null}} filling whatever is missing; format.model.setStyle(sheet, addrs, patch) -> new sheet with the patch merged into each address's style. history.model.empty() -> a fresh stack; history.model.push(stack, state) -> new stack with state on top of the past and the redo branch cleared, keeping at most 50 past states; history.model.undo(stack, current) -> {stack, state}: the most recent past state becomes state and current goes to the redo branch, with nothing to undo returns {stack, state: current}; history.model.redo(stack, current) -> {stack, state} the reverse; history.model.canUndo(stack), history.model.canRedo(stack) -> booleans; history.model.depth(stack) -> number of past states. rowscols.model.insertRow(sheet, row) -> new sheet where the 1-based row and everything below moves down one, cells, formats and rules included, and every formula of THIS sheet has its references and ranges to moved cells rewritten; rowscols.model.deleteRow(sheet, row) -> new sheet without that row, rows below moved up, a reference to a deleted cell replaced by #REF! in the formula text, a range shrinking when it loses a row and becoming #REF! when it loses every row; rowscols.model.insertCol(sheet, col), rowscols.model.deleteCol(sheet, col) -> the same for a 0-based column. References into other sheets and formulas of other sheets are left as they are. fill.model.series(seed, count) -> count raw strings continuing the seed: one number continues by 1, two numbers set the step, a YYYY-MM-DD date continues by one day, anything else repeats the last seed; fill.model.shiftFormula(raw, dRow, dCol) -> the formula with every relative reference part moved (a $ before a column letter or a row number fixes that part, a cross-sheet reference shifts too) and a reference pushed off the sheet replaced by #REF!; fill.model.fillDown(sheet, 'A2:A4') -> new sheet where each row of the range below the first holds the first row's cells, formulas shifted by the row distance, values copied. find.model.find(sheet, query, {matchCase, inFormulas}) -> [{addr, raw}] of the cells whose raw text contains query, in row-major order, case-insensitive unless matchCase, formula cells skipped unless inFormulas (both false by default); find.model.replace(sheet, query, replacement, opts) -> {sheet, count}: every occurrence replaced in every matching cell, count the number of cells changed. csv.model.toCSV(rows) -> text: rows joined with newline, fields with comma, a field holding a comma, a double quote or a newline wrapped in double quotes with inner quotes doubled, no trailing newline; csv.model.parse(text) -> rows of strings honouring quotes, doubled quotes, embedded newlines and CRLF, '' -> []; csv.model.exportRange(sheet, 'A1:B3', values) -> rows of general display strings of the sheet's computed values; csv.model.paste(sheet, addr, rows) -> new sheet with the rows written as raw texts from addr rightwards and downwards. chart.model.series(values, labelsRange, dataRange) -> {labels: [display strings], data: [numbers, a non-number counting as 0], max}; chart.model.svg(series, {width, height}) -> an SVG string starting with <svg, one <rect ... height="N"> per value with heights proportional to value / max, and one <text> label per bar. validation.model.check(rule, raw) -> [] or one message per failing rule: {kind: 'number', min, max} needs a number within the bounds, {kind: 'list', values} needs one of the values, {kind: 'date'} needs a real YYYY-MM-DD date; validation.model.setRule(sheet, addr, rule) -> new sheet; validation.model.violations(sheet) -> [{addr, errors}] in address order over the cells with a rule whose raw text fails, formula cells never checked, valid cells left out. names.model.validate(name, book) -> error strings: blank, not matching /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/, looking like a cell address, already defined (case-insensitive); names.model.define(book, name, target) -> new book; names.model.resolve(book, name) -> the target or null, case-insensitive; names.model.remove(book, name) -> new book. sheets.model.add(book, name) -> new book with a sheet {id unique, name, cells: {}, formats: {}, rules: {}, conditional: []} appended; sheets.model.rename(book, id, name), sheets.model.remove(book, id) -> new books, the last sheet never removed (the book comes back as is); sheets.model.validate(name, book) -> errors: blank, holding ! or :, already used (case-insensitive); sheets.model.byName(book, name) -> the sheet or null, case-insensitive. conditional.model.matches(rule, value) -> boolean for {kind: 'gt' | 'lt' | 'between' | 'eq' | 'contains', value, value2, cls}: gt, lt, between (inclusive) and eq compare numbers and never match a non-number, contains matches a string case-insensitively; conditional.model.addRule(sheet, rule) -> new sheet with the rule appended to sheet.conditional; conditional.model.classes(sheet, values) -> {ADDR: [cls]} for the cells of each rule's range whose value matches, cells with no match left out. stats.model.summary(values, range) -> {count, sum, avg, min, max, cells}: count, sum, avg, min, max over the numbers of the range (avg, min, max null and sum 0 without any), cells the number of non-null values. persist.model.KEY -> the localStorage key; persist.model.save(book) writes JSON {version: 2, sheets, active, names} under KEY; persist.model.load() -> {version, sheets, active, names} or null when nothing is stored, migrating a version-1 document first; persist.model.migrate(doc) -> a version-2 document: a version-1 document is {version: 1, cells: {ADDR: raw}} for one sheet and becomes one sheet named Sheet1 holding those cells as {raw}, with empty formats, rules and conditional, active pointing at it and names {}; a version-2 document is returned as is. keys.model.next(addr, key, bounds) -> the address after the key: 'ArrowUp' | 'ArrowDown' | 'ArrowLeft' | 'ArrowRight', 'Enter' (down), 'Tab' (right), 'Shift+Tab' (left), 'Home' (column A), 'Ctrl+Home' (A1), anything else unchanged, clamped to bounds {cols, rows} counted from A1; keys.model.selection(anchor, focus) -> the normalised range 'A1:C3' from any two corners; keys.model.inRange(addr, range) -> boolean.
skeleton: Spreadsheet
